name: Thai Universal Dependency Treebank
description: Automatic dependency parsing of Thai sentences has been underexplored, as evidenced by the lack of large Thai dependency treebanks with complete dependency structures and the lack of a published systematic evaluation of state-of-the-art models, especially transformer-based parsers. In this work, we address these problems by introducing Thai Universal Dependency Treebank (TUD), a new largest Thai treebank consisting of 3,627 trees annotated in accordance with the Universal Dependencies (UD) framework. We then benchmark dependency parsing models that incorporate pretrained transformers as encoders and train them on Thai-PUD and our TUD. The evaluation results show that most of our models can outperform other models reported in previous papers and provide insight into the optimal choices of components to include in Thai dependency parsers. The new treebank and every model's full prediction generated in our experiment are made available on a GitHub repository for further study.
reputation: A language-specific Universal Dependencies treebank that is useful for Thai parsing research, though it is a niche benchmark rather than a broad community standard.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark for syntactic parsing; relatively small treebank (3,627 trees) and results are parser-dependent, with evaluation typically reported as labeled and unlabeled attachment scores.
